key_insight: PhySGA grounds 3D object composition in physical-space reasoning rather than relying only on static digital priors. This makes 3D scene assembly more generalizable, interactive, and better suited to challenging real-world constraints.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of composing multiple 3D objects accurately in complex scenes, where prior methods struggle with precise placement, physical consistency, and generalization beyond simple layouts.
method: Uses a physics-space grounded agentic framework to reason about object composition in physically meaningful coordinates.
Combines agent-like decision making with 3D spatial constraints to improve placement quality and interaction support.
Targets generalizable composition across diverse scenes instead of depending on fixed coordinate prediction or image-synthesis priors.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more robust path to 3D content creation and robot simulation by aligning composition with physical reality. It can improve downstream tasks that need accurate, interactive, and transferable scene assembly.

paper_title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition
paper_authors: Weichen Lyu, Chong Xia, Mingyu Dong, Long Xu, Shengjun Zhang
